findings.description: When the native setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate/requestAnimationFrame returns a non-number that is also null or undefined (some polyfills or browsers do this, and the old code explicitly guarded for it), the new else branch evaluates `handleOrId.refresh`. That throws a TypeError inside scheduleTask, so scheduling crashes where it previously worked and returned the task.

The code now uses truthiness checks (`if (handleId)`) instead of `typeof === 'number'`. A numeric handle of 0 is treated as no handle, so it is never stored in tasksByHandleId and is not cleaned up. clearTimeout(0) then cannot find the task, and the function returns the task object instead of 0.

In scheduleTask, any non-number result from the native setter is assumed to be an object, so `handleOrId.refresh` is read unconditionally. The old code explicitly allowed setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate and requestAnimationFrame to return undefined or null (polyfills or odd environments). With such a return value this now throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'refresh')` while scheduling, which is a regression. The lookup should be guarded, for example with `handleOrId?.refresh`.

The scoping state (`_safeSelector` and `_shouldScopeIndicator`) is stored as mutable instance fields shared across recursive `_scopeSelector` and `_applySelectorScope` calls. Nested pseudo-function calls (`isParentSelector` false) can change `_shouldScopeIndicator`, which the outer call then reads for its remaining parts. For example, a `:host` inside `:is()`/`:where()` can flip scoping for later sibling parts or comma alternatives. Edge cases such as `:where(:host) .a, .b` or several nested pseudo functions in one selector could be scoped or left unscoped incorrectly. Nesting also depends on `_safeSelector` not being replaced mid-call.

`_pseudoFunctionAwareScopeSelectorPart` treats any part that starts with `:where(` or `:is(` as if it also ends with the matching `)`. It slices off the last character with `slice(prefix.length, -1)` and then appends `)`. For a part with a suffix after the function, such as `:is(.foo):hover`, `:where(.a).b` or `:where(a):where(b)`, the slice drops a character that is not the closing paren. The inner text is then scoped incorrectly and a stray `)` is appended. For example, `:is(.foo):hover` is rewritten around the inner text `.foo):hove`, which gives broken or incorrect CSS. The concatenated-pseudo case is only papered over in the tests, where an `xit` documents the wrong output.

The new `ts_test_library` and `karma_web_test_suite` targets are appended, but this hunk adds no matching `load(...)` statements, unlike the ng-debug-api BUILD file. If the lib BUILD file does not already load these symbols, Bazel analysis of the package fails and breaks every target in it.

The afterRenderEffect tracks componentExplorerView and diDebugAPIsAvailable. It calls init() on every run, so each new explorer view re-registers the 'highlightComponent' message-bus listener, producing duplicate handlers. It also re-creates both InjectorTreeVisualizers each time, which discards zoom/pan state and may leave selectedNode pointing at stale nodes. The listener setup and visualizer creation should run once, not on every update.

The component defines sortedProviders (sorted by token), but the template still passes the raw providers() input to ng-injector-providers. Providers are therefore no longer sorted alphabetically, which regresses the previous behaviour where they were sorted before being set.

Tabs are now hidden with the [hidden] attribute instead of a CSS class with display:none. The tab components set :host { display: block/flex } in their own styles, which overrides the browser's [hidden] rule. Inactive tabs, such as the Components explorer, may therefore stay visible and render alongside the active tab.

The afterRenderEffect write callback runs on every `componentExplorerView` change, and it calls `init()` each time. Each call registers another `highlightComponent` message-bus listener, so listeners accumulate and the highlight handler fires multiple times. It also re-runs `setUpEnvironmentInjectorVisualizer` and `setUpElementInjectorVisualizer` on every update, which recreates both D3 visualizers. That discards zoom and pan state and any rendered graph on each forest update. Initialization used to run once.

The template passes `providers()` to `ng-injector-providers`. The sorted `sortedProviders` computed is never used, and the parent now sets the raw unsorted list. Providers are therefore no longer sorted by token, which regresses the previous behavior.

Visibility is now toggled with the `hidden` attribute and the `.hidden` CSS class is removed. The `hidden` attribute only maps to the UA stylesheet's `display:none`. Any component whose `:host` sets `display` (block or flex) overrides it, so inactive tabs may stay visible. The old `.hidden` class was needed for exactly this reason. In addition, the injector tree previously used `visibility:hidden` with `position:absolute` so D3 could still measure layout while hidden. Under `display:none`, later graph updates while the tab is hidden may compute wrong sizes.

`diDebugAPIsAvailable` is now computed from the current view. It is false whenever the view is null or the forest is empty. The 'only available on version 17.0.0 or higher' message therefore shows before the first view arrives, or when the forest is temporarily empty. The `@else` branch also destroys the whole tree DOM in that case. Previously the flag was only ever set to true and never reverted.

The zone.js file was moved from `@npm//:node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js` to the `//:node_modules/zone.js` target, so pkg_web now publishes it under `node_modules/zone.js/...` instead of `npm/node_modules/zone.js/...`. The index.html for this devapp is not updated in this diff, unlike demo-standalone. It probably still loads `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js`, which would 404 and leave the dev app without zone.js. The `tslib.js` entry was also removed from the same pkg_web, so anything that still references it would break too.

The static files now ship zone.js via `//:node_modules/zone.js`, which changes the output path from `npm/node_modules/...`. The shell-browser index.html and any manifest or packaging step that references the old `npm/node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js` path are not updated in this diff. The extension page could therefore fail to load zone.js.

The zone.js source changes from `@npm//:node_modules/zone.js/...` to `//:node_modules/zone.js`. This changes where the file lands in the pkg_web output, from `npm/node_modules/...` to `node_modules/...`. The matching change to `devtools/src/index.html` is not in this diff, whereas demo-standalone's index.html was updated. If index.html still references `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js`, the dev app will fail to load zone.js with a 404 and break at runtime. The `tslib.js` removal also relies on nothing else referencing it.

The zone.js dependency was moved to the workspace target `//:node_modules/zone.js`, which changes the output path from `npm/node_modules/...` to `node_modules/...`. The shell-browser `index.html` is not updated in this diff. If it still points at the `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/...` path, the extension shell will not find zone.js.

`lookup_field` now returns the final related field `f` for `a__b` lookups, but callers such as `items_for_result` assume `f` belongs to the row object. For a ForeignKey final field (`remote_field` is a `ManyToOneRel`), `items_for_result` calls `getattr(result, f.name)` on the wrong model. That raises `AttributeError` or shows the wrong value, for example for `list_display = ['parent__parent']`. Previously `f` was always `None` on this path, so the value was rendered correctly.

`get_fields_from_path(opts.model, name)` is called whenever the attribute traversal succeeds and the name contains `__`. If the final segment is a property or method on the related model rather than a model field, the traversal succeeds but `get_fields_from_path` raises `FieldDoesNotExist` or `NotRelationField`. The unguarded exception turns a previously working display into a crash, for example `list_display` with `'parent__some_property'` or custom attribute paths.

`get_fields_from_path(opts.model, name)[-1]` is called unconditionally for any `__` name that resolves through the `getattr` traversal. The traversal also resolves properties, methods and reverse accessors on the related object, for example `parent__some_property`. `get_fields_from_path` only handles real model fields, so for those names it raises `FieldDoesNotExist` or `NotRelationField`. The exception is raised inside the `except` handler, so it is not caught and the changelist crashes with a 500. Previously these names rendered fine. A related ForeignKey or relation as the final field also now gets a non-None `f`, which changes how `items_for_result` renders the value. The call is also indented inside the `for part` loop, so it runs on every iteration instead of once after the loop.

For `fk__exact` search fields, `prev_field` is the ForeignKey, so `validate_field.formfield().to_python(bit)` goes through `ModelChoiceField.to_python`. That runs a database query (`queryset.get(...)`) for every search term and every such field. It also routes the lookup through the related model's default manager and `to_field_name`, so objects hidden by a custom default manager raise ValidationError and are silently skipped. The old Cast-based approach did no per-term queries and applied no manager filtering. Search results can therefore differ, and each search issues extra queries.

A search field like `fk__exact` makes `prev_field` the ForeignKey. Its `formfield()` is a `ModelChoiceField`, and `to_python` on it runs a database query for every search term. It also applies `limit_choices_to` and the field's queryset, so valid values outside that queryset are silently skipped. It returns a model instance instead of the raw value. The old Cast approach did none of this. This adds N queries per search and can change results for relation exact lookups. For these fields, validation should use the model field's own `to_python`/`get_prep_value`, or the related target field, rather than the form field.

The rewrite changes how newlines are handled. Each line from `splitlines(True)` goes through `TextWrapper.wrap()`, and the results are joined with '
'. `wrap()` returns an empty list for blank or whitespace-only lines such as '
', so blank lines and paragraph breaks are dropped. For example, 'a

b' becomes 'a
b'. A trailing newline is also stripped, so 'abc
' becomes 'abc'. The old implementation preserved both, so `wordwrap` output for multi-paragraph text regresses. In addition, `TextWrapper` collapses tabs and other whitespace by default (`replace_whitespace=True`), and this was not done before.

The rewrite changes behavior for newlines and whitespace. `wrapper.wrap(line)` returns `[]` for empty or whitespace-only lines, so blank lines, including paragraph separators like `

`, are silently dropped. `splitlines(True)` keeps the trailing `
`, but `TextWrapper` replaces it with a space and then drops it, so a trailing newline in the input is lost. Whitespace-only lines and leading or trailing whitespace are also removed. Existing `wordwrap` behavior, which preserved these, regresses; for example `wrap('a

b', 10)` now returns `'a
b'`.

The check `".." in str(filter_expression.var)` also matches quoted string literals and translated constants, not just variable lookups. A template such as `{{ "Loading..." }}` or `{{ "a..b"|upper }}` has no double-dot lookup, but it now emits a RemovedInDjango70Warning. Once the deprecation ends, the commented-out code would raise TemplateSyntaxError for these valid templates. The check should only apply to real variable lookups, not literals.

The check `".." in str(filter_expression.var)` also matches constant string literals, not just variable lookups. For a literal like `{{ "Loading..." }}` or `{{ "a..b"|upper }}`, FilterExpression resolves the constant, so `.var` is the plain string and contains "..". Translated literals such as `{{ _("Loading...") }}` also match, since Variable.var keeps the raw text. These valid templates get a spurious deprecation warning. Once the deprecation ends and the check becomes an error, they would raise TemplateSyntaxError.

`self.origin.name` is dereferenced without checking for None. Parser accepts `origin=None`, so a Parser constructed directly without an origin and given a template with `..` raises AttributeError instead of the warning.

The old single-column case used a plain `field__in` lookup. That lookup deduplicated values, skipped NULLs, and chunked IN lists for backends with `max_in_list_size` (Oracle). It now always builds a `TupleIn` over a one-element `ColPairs`, even for ordinary single-column FKs, and passes all instance keys as one-element tuples. This pushes every simple forward-FK prefetch through the tuple lookup path. On backends without tuple-lookup support, the result is a large OR-of-ANDs expression that can exceed expression-depth or in-list limits. Instances whose FK is NULL now put `(None,)` into the list, which the old code would not do cleanly. Single-field prefetches can therefore regress in SQL shape and robustness.

`ColPairs` is built with `queryset.model._meta.db_table` as the alias, not the query's actual base alias. If the supplied prefetch queryset already carries a custom alias or an earlier join/combinator, the column references may point at a table alias that does not exist in the query. That would produce wrong SQL or an error.

Replacing `writer_name="html"` with `writer="html"` is only safe on docutils 0.22+, where the `writer` argument accepts a name string. On older supported versions, `writer` must be a Writer instance, and `writer_name` is what selects the writer. A string passed as `writer` is kept as-is, so the writer name falls back to the default 'pseudoxml' or the call fails with an AttributeError when the Publisher calls the writer's methods. That would break `parse_rst`, and so the admindocs views, for users on older docutils. The change needs a version check or has to keep `writer_name` for older docutils.

The new <button> elements are created without type="button", so they default to type="submit" inside the admin form. The click handlers currently call e.preventDefault(), which prevents submission. Any path that bypasses those handlers, such as a handler change or a click that does not reach them, would submit the form. Setting type="button" would be more robust.

The local-field check uses `self.fields`, which keeps the '-' prefix on descending fields (e.g. `fields=['-name']`). The old code used `fields_orders`, which strips the prefix. Now `_check_local_fields` looks up the field '-name' and reports a bogus 'refers to the nonexistent field' error (models.E012) for valid descending indexes. The fields are also put in a set, so error ordering is nondeterministic.

W037 is computed with `any(self.condition is not None for index in model._meta.indexes)`. The generator ignores `index` and checks `self.condition`, so every index on the model gets the warning if the current index has a condition, and none do otherwise. Because the feature checks now run per index, W037, W040 and W043 are each emitted once per index instead of once per model and database. A model with several indexes gets duplicate warnings, and the W037 condition is wrong when only some indexes have conditions.

All index checks, including name validation (E033/E034) and nonexistent, M2M, or non-local field validation, now run only inside the `for db in databases` loop and only for databases where `allow_migrate_model` is true. Previously these checks ran unconditionally. With `databases=None`/empty (e.g. `Model.check()`) or when migration is disallowed, invalid index names and fields go unreported. The same errors are also repeated once per database. The test changes passing `databases=self.databases` mask this regression.

The field check uses `self.fields`, which keeps the raw names including the `-` prefix for descending indexes (e.g. `fields=['-name']`). The original code used `fields_orders`, which strips the prefix. `_check_local_fields` will now report a nonexistent field `-name` (models.E012) for every valid descending index, a false-positive regression. It should use the names from `self.fields_orders`.

The feature checks (W037, W040, W043) were moved into a per-index method but still iterate over all `model._meta.indexes`. A model with several indexes will emit the same W040/W043 warning once per index, even for indexes that don't use the feature. The W037 generator also reads `self.condition` instead of `index.condition`, so the `any()` is meaningless. Previously each warning was emitted once per model and database. The checks should test only `self`.

Index name and field checks (E033, E034, E012 etc.) now run only inside the per-database loop. If `databases` is empty or None, or the router disallows migrating the model on every database, these database-independent checks are silently skipped. They previously always ran. With several databases, the same errors are also repeated once per database.

`relatedWindows` is declared in this file as a block-scoped `const relatedWindows = []`, so it is not a property of `window`. Changing the references to `window.relatedWindows` means `window.relatedWindows` is `undefined` in production. `dismissRelatedLookupPopup` then throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'indexOf')` after setting the value and before `win.close()`. The raw-id lookup popup therefore never closes, and the real `relatedWindows` list is never cleaned up. The new test hides the bug by defining `window.relatedWindows` in `beforeEach`.

The code now reads `window.relatedWindows`, but the file keeps the array as a local `const relatedWindows` inside the IIFE. If that is still the case, `window.relatedWindows` is undefined in production. Selecting a value in a raw-id popup would then throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'indexOf')` before `win.close()` runs, so the popup would not close. The new test hides this by setting `window.relatedWindows = window.relatedWindows || []` in `beforeEach`.

The change is described as fixing #31170 by triggering a `change` event after the value is set, but no event is triggered. The diff only swaps `document.getElementById(name).value` for `elem.value`, which is functionally identical. Dependent fields still do not update, so the ticket's behavior is not fixed.

In the insert path, an expression-valued field is appended to `returning_fields` without checking whether it is already there. `meta.db_returning_fields` already contains fields with a `db_default`. If such a field is given an expression (e.g. `Now()`) on insert, it appears twice in `returning_fields`. That gives a duplicated column in the RETURNING clause, and the returned value is assigned twice. On backends without insert RETURNING, the field list is misaligned with the returned values. A membership check (`if field not in returning_fields`) is needed.

In the insert path, a field whose value is an expression is appended to returning_fields without checking whether it is already there. A field that is already in meta.db_returning_fields (for example one with a db_default or db_returning=True) and is assigned an expression ends up listed twice. The INSERT ... RETURNING clause then contains duplicate columns, and _assign_returned_values pairs the returned values with the wrong fields or sets the field twice. The append needs a `field not in returning_fields` guard.

get_supported_language_variant() now raises ValueError for over-long codes. Callers that pass unbounded, user-controlled input only catch LookupError. get_language_from_path() is one: its regex `\w+([@-]\w+){0,2}` has no length limit. A request such as `/xxxx…(>500 chars)/` handled by LocaleMiddleware or i18n_patterns, with no hyphen in the prefix or with strict=True, now raises an uncaught ValueError and returns a 500 instead of None or a 404. The new exception is a regression for existing callers.

get_supported_language_variant() now raises ValueError for over-long codes. Callers that only catch LookupError are not updated. get_language_from_path() passes the URL prefix matched by language_code_prefix_re, and that prefix can be arbitrarily long (\w+). A request path such as /xxxx…(over 500 chars)/ makes LocaleMiddleware and i18n_patterns raise an uncaught ValueError, which returns a 500 instead of a 404 or None. The same applies to any other caller that handles only LookupError.

The UNNEST path builds the cast from `field.db_type()` for every non-array field. That breaks for fields whose `db_type` is not a valid array element type. AutoField/BigAutoField/SmallAutoField return `serial`/`bigserial`, and `(%s)::serial[]` is invalid SQL, so a bulk_create with explicit pk values now raises a ProgrammingError. Other field types also fail: JSONField (the Jsonb adapter can't be sent as an array element), range and hstore fields, and GIS geometry fields with a custom placeholder. This path also ignores `field.get_placeholder()`. Only array fields are excluded, so previously working bulk_create calls can now crash or insert wrong data.

The UNNEST path builds casts from `field.db_type()` instead of `cast_db_type()`. For AutoField, BigAutoField and SmallAutoField, `db_type` returns `serial`, `bigserial` or `smallserial`. These are not valid cast targets, so `(%s)::serial[]` is a PostgreSQL syntax error. `bulk_create` with two or more objects that set explicit primary keys on an auto field, or an insert that includes such a field, will crash instead of inserting.

The array check uses `endswith("[]")`, which misses ArrayField with a size, whose `db_type` is e.g. `integer[5]`. Such fields are not excluded, so UNNEST flattens the nested array values and the insert fails or inserts wrong data. The check should be `endswith("]")`.

_create_alternatives now reads `alternative.content` and `alternative.mimetype`. Existing code that appends plain tuples directly, e.g. `msg.alternatives.append((html, 'text/html'))` or `msg.alternatives = [(html, 'text/html')]` after construction, now raises AttributeError in message()/send(). Previously `_create_mime_attachment(*alternative)` accepted any 2-sequence. Unpacking with `*alternative` would have kept backward compatibility. Likewise, `Alternative(*alternative)` in __init__ now raises TypeError at construction for malformed items.

If a user passes max_length=None to the form GenericIPAddressField, setdefault keeps the None. to_python then calls clean_ipv6_address(..., max_length=None) for any value containing ':', and `len(ip_str) > None` raises TypeError instead of validating. This used to work, so it is a regression for callers who explicitly disabled max_length.

If a user explicitly passes max_length=None to the form GenericIPAddressField, setdefault keeps None and to_python passes it to clean_ipv6_address. There `len(ip_str) > None` raises TypeError for any value containing ':'. This used to work, so it is a crash and a regression for existing code that disables the length limit.

The SelectBox cache guard checks `SelectBox.cache[currentSelect.id]` instead of the target `select.id`. When a filter_horizontal popup add calls this function with `toElem`, that cache entry always exists, so the guard is false. Any other filter_horizontal "from" box for the same model then gets the new option in the DOM only, not in the SelectBox cache. The option disappears on the next redisplay, such as filtering or moving items. The check is also unrelated to the select being updated.

The cache guard checks `SelectBox.cache[currentSelect.id]`, but the code then calls `add_to_cache` and `redisplay` on `select.id`. When the popup was opened from a plain FK select, `currentSelect` has no cache entry, so the condition is true. Then, whenever `SelectBox` is loaded (any filter_horizontal widget on the page), the code runs against another plain select for the same model that has no cache entry. `SelectBox.add_to_cache` does `SelectBox.cache[id].push(...)` on an undefined cache and throws a TypeError. That aborts the update loop and the rest of the popup dismissal. The guard should test `SelectBox.cache[select.id]` and require it to exist.

The message is %-formatted with min_length before it is passed to ngettext(), so the msgid becomes e.g. 'This password is too short. It must contain at least 8 characters.' instead of the template with '%(min_length)d'. That string does not exist in any translation catalog, so the lookup fails and the error always appears in English. This regresses translations of the MinimumLengthValidator error for every non-English locale. The interpolation should happen after translation.

The `params={'min_length': ...}` argument was removed from the ValidationError. Code that reads `error.params['min_length']` or relies on the message being lazily interpolated from params now gets None or a KeyError. This is a backward-compatibility regression for existing users.

MinimumLengthValidator now interpolates min_length with `%` before passing the strings to ngettext. The message ids become e.g. 'at least 8 characters.' instead of the template 'at least %(min_length)d characters.' that exists in the locale catalogs. Translation lookup therefore fails, and the too-short error is always shown in English for non-English locales. This is a regression from the previous behavior. The `params={'min_length': ...}` argument was also dropped, so code that reads `error.params['min_length']` no longer works.

pre_migrate.connect is called without sender=self. pre_migrate is emitted once per app config, so rename_permissions runs once per installed app. Each run inserts another RenamePermission after every RenameModel in the same plan, which leaves duplicate operations. The duplicates run repeatedly, and on backward migrations they are redundant. The handler should be connected with sender=self, as the contenttypes equivalent does.

The ContentType filter uses model__icontains=old_model.lower(), a substring match, instead of an exact match. Renaming model 'Foo' also matches content types such as 'foobar' or 'myfoo' in the same app. Permissions of unrelated models are then renamed to the new model's codenames.

The codename prefix is taken with split('_')[0] and every permission is rewritten to '<prefix>_<newmodel>' with name 'Can <prefix> ...'. Custom permissions such as 'can_publish_foo' or 'publish_foo' are corrupted or collide. For example, 'can_publish_foo' becomes 'can_newmodel'. Only the default add/change/delete/view permissions should be renamed.

The queries use the default manager (Permission.objects, and ContentType via apps) and ignore the schema editor's database alias `db`. With multiple databases, the rename reads from and writes to the default database instead of the one being migrated. Only the atomic block uses `using=db`; the save() does not pass using=db.
IntegrityError is swallowed silently, so a conflicting permission leaves the old permission stale with no warning. The new_name comparison also overwrites any customized permission names.

The content type lookup uses `model__icontains=old_model.lower()`, a substring match, instead of an exact match. Renaming `User` to `Customer` also selects content types such as `userprofile` or `superuser` in the same app. Their permissions are then renamed to `add_customer` and so on. This corrupts unrelated models' permissions, and the IntegrityError handler only hides some of the collisions. It should be `model=old_model.lower()`.

Every permission on the content type is rewritten as `<first word of codename>_<newmodel>` with a generated name. Custom permissions from `Meta.permissions` (e.g. `can_publish_oldmodel`, which becomes `can_newmodel`) are clobbered. Permission names built from a custom `verbose_name` are overwritten with the CamelCase-derived default. Only the default add/change/delete/view permissions should be renamed.

The query and save use the default router (`Permission.objects` and `permission.save()` without `using=db`), while only the atomic block uses `schema_editor.connection.alias`. When migrating a non-default database, this reads and writes the wrong database, or the update happens outside the intended transaction. The queryset should use `.using(db)` and the save should pass `using=db`.

The new MRO walk collects every property found in any class in the MRO. It does not skip names that a subclass overrides with a non-property, such as a field, a method or a plain attribute. The old getattr_static approach only looked at the first definition in the MRO. A parent `@property foo` overridden in a child by a non-property is therefore wrongly listed in `_property_names`. Code that relies on this set (Model.__init__ kwargs handling, QuerySet get_or_create/update_or_create param extraction) will then treat the name as a property, which gives wrong results. The fix is to track names already seen in more-derived classes and ignore properties that were shadowed.

The new MRO walk collects every property found in any class's __dict__ without tracking names already shadowed by a more-derived class. The old code used getattr_static, which resolved to the first match in the MRO. If a base class defines a property and a subclass overrides that name with a non-property (a model field, a plain attribute, or None), the name is still reported as a property. Because _property_names is used to decide which names clash with field names, and by QuerySet.update_or_create/get_or_create to reject property names, this can wrongly reject valid kwargs or raise errors for overridden attributes. The fix is to keep a 'seen' set of all names from more-derived classes and skip those.

Subquery.resolve_expression only catches AttributeError around `self.output_field`. When the wrapped query has no explicit single select column (e.g. `Subquery(Model.objects.all())` before default columns are added) and no explicit output_field, `Query.output_field` returns None. The cached `output_field` property then raises FieldError ("Cannot resolve expression type, unknown output_field"), not AttributeError. The exception escapes from resolve_expression, so such Subquery expressions now crash at resolution time. Previously the output field was resolved lazily and the expression worked when it was never needed.
